Cross-Cap

Cross-Cap is a topological surface, given by a parametrisation, immersed with singularities.

About

The projective plane rendered with a single segment of self-intersection ending in two pinch points. It is the crudest of the three standard pictures -- Boy's surface is smooth and the Roman surface is symmetric -- and the easiest to see through: a disc with its boundary glued to itself the wrong way round.

Definition

the standard cross-cap immersion of RP^2; antipodes (u + pi, -v) map to the same point, so the hemisphere v >= 0 covers the surface once
